ELI5: Why is it common practice to require math students to rationalize the denominator for a fraction to be considered in simplest form?

The shallow reason is when you are grading lots of math, it is easier to verify students' answers if they are all in the same form.

The deeper reason is that numbers with rational denominators are easier to estimate because it is easier to divide by rational numbers than real numbers. I get a clearer impression of a number with a rationalized denominator, so I prefer it aesthetically.

With sqrt(3) ~ 1.73, which is easier to estimate by eyballing it?

1.73 / 3

or

1 / 1.73

That's interesting--it is easier to estimate with the rational denominator. I suspected the grade thing played a role as well but I wondered if there was some deeper reason that dividing by an irrational number was considered less simplified. So would it be fair to say that rationalizing your denominators is the equivalent of having good math manners?
Yes. People appreciate not needing to think too hard. Anything you can do to reduce that is kindness.

It depends on the situation. When dealing with purely numerical answers (i.e. sqrt(3)/3) it's polite and advantageous because you can quickly eyeball it, but once you're into higher math the benefits quickly fade away - sqrt(x)/x isn't much of an improvement over 1/sqrt(x), and when calculators are the norm rationalizing just ends up creating extra operations. If I just wanted to throw in some values for x, the non-rationalized version will be quicker and less error-prone, especially if x is something other than a small integer. Likewise, if the formula is going to be used in a computer program or similar rationalizing may create inefficiency.

The golden rule is "use whatever format is going to be most convenient for your reader (or whichever one they ask for, because there's no accounting for taste)."
